suggestions.clause: Scope of the Agreement; Work Orders; Nature of Services; Transfer of Obligations
suggestions.reason: The use of "may include" renders the scope of Services non-exhaustive and permissive rather than definitively bounded, exposing Quintiles, Inc. to claims by Sponsor that additional or unspecified activities fall within the Agreement's coverage and are therefore owed without a separate Work Order. The absence of any exclusion for services not described in a Work Order compounds this risk, as Sponsor could assert that the open-ended category of "other research and development services" draws broadly unspecified obligations into scope, potentially triggering performance, liability, and payment disputes that Quintiles, Inc. cannot readily defeat on the face of the Agreement. Because the operative scope of each engagement should be governed exclusively by the relevant Work Order, the definition must be amended to cap scope at what is expressly documented and to make clear that services not so described are excluded.
suggestions.original_text: Nature of Services. The services covered by this Agreement may include expert consultation, clinical trial services, statistical programming and analysis, clerical, project management, central laboratory services, preclinical services, pharmaceutical sciences services, and related data processing, data management and regulatory services, and other research and development services requested by Sponsor and agreed to by Quintiles as set forth in the relevant Work Order (collectively, the “Services”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Nature of Services. The services covered by this Agreement are limited to expert consultation, clinical trial services, statistical programming and analysis, clerical, project management, central laboratory services, preclinical services, pharmaceutical sciences services, and related data processing, data management and regulatory services, and other research and development services expressly requested by Sponsor and agreed to by Quintiles as set forth in the relevant Work Order (collectively, the "Services"). Any services not expressly described in a Work Order are excluded from this Agreement and shall not constitute Services hereunder.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause creates material financial exposure for Quintiles, Inc. by omitting a late-payment remedy: Sponsor faces no interest, suspension right, or other consequence for delayed payment, leaving Quintiles without leverage to accelerate collection. The dispute-resolution obligation is anchored only to "as soon as practicable," which is commercially unenforceable and could allow Sponsor to hold disputed amounts indefinitely without consequence. Additionally, the clause does not require each Work Order to specify the fee calculation basis, meaning the methodology by which fees are earned is undocumented at the master agreement level, which could expose Quintiles to fee challenges if a Work Order is ambiguous or silent on that point.
suggestions.original_text: Payment of Fees and Expenses. Sponsor will pay Quintiles for fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the budget and payment schedule contained in each Work Order. Sponsor agrees that the budget and payment schedule for each Work Order will be structured in an effort to maintain cash neutrality for Quintiles (with respect to the payment of professional fees, pass-through costs and otherwise). Unless otherwise agreed in a particular Work Order, the following shall apply: (a) Quintiles will invoice Sponsor monthly for the fees, expenses and pass-through costs incurred in performing the Services; and, (b) Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt of the invoice. If any portion of an invoice is disputed, then Sponsor shall pay the undisputed amounts as set forth in the preceding sentence and the parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile the disputed amount as soon as practicable.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Payment of Fees and Expenses. Sponsor will pay Quintiles for fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the budget and payment schedule contained in each Work Order, which shall specify the applicable fee calculation basis (whether fixed-fee, time-and-materials, or otherwise). Sponsor agrees that the budget and payment schedule for each Work Order will be structured in an effort to maintain cash neutrality for Quintiles (with respect to the payment of professional fees, pass-through costs and otherwise). Unless otherwise agreed in a particular Work Order, the following shall apply: (a) Quintiles will invoice Sponsor monthly for the fees, expenses and pass-through costs incurred in performing the Services; and, (b) Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt of the invoice. Any amounts not paid by the due date shall accrue interest at a rate of one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less. If any portion of an invoice is disputed, then Sponsor shall pay the undisputed amounts as set forth in the preceding sentence and the parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile the disputed amount within thirty (30) days of Sponsor's written notice of such dispute.

suggestions.reason: The Term clause does no more than state a five-year duration and defer entirely to Section 15, without itself specifying that termination must be effected by written notice, when it takes effect, or what grounds support it, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed to an oral or informal termination with immediate effect and no contractual basis to insist on a cure period before the Agreement ends. Without any reference to consequences upon termination—such as payment for work performed, return of Quintiles, Inc.'s materials, or refund of prepaid amounts—the clause creates material financial exposure for Quintiles, Inc. if the counterparty terminates and retains the benefit of services rendered or funds advanced. The absence of any reference to surviving provisions and transition obligations is a further gap: key protections such as confidentiality, intellectual property, and indemnification obligations would have no express textual anchor securing them post-termination. Section 15 must be drafted to address these elements in full; the Term clause should, at minimum, direct it to do so.
suggestions.original_text: Term. This Agreement shall commence on the date it has been signed by all parties and shall continue for a period of five (5) years from the date of execution, unless otherwise earlier terminated by either party in accordance with Section 15 below.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Term. This Agreement shall commence on the date it has been signed by all parties and shall continue for a period of five (5) years from the date of execution, unless earlier terminated by written notice in accordance with Section 15 below, which shall address the grounds for termination, applicable cure rights, required notice periods, the effective date of termination, consequences upon termination, surviving provisions, and any required transition obligations.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Quintiles, Inc. to three material risks: (i) it restricts the written amendment requirement solely to Work Orders, leaving the broader Agreement, schedules, and exhibits potentially modifiable without a formal Change Order process; (ii) it does not identify who holds authority to execute a Change Order on behalf of each party, meaning an unauthorized employee could bind Quintiles to scope, budget, or timeline changes; and (iii) the absence of an anti-oral-modification provision means that informal communications, emails, or course-of-dealing conduct could be argued to constitute binding amendments, undermining Quintiles' right to postpone implementing changes until a Change Order is executed. Left uncorrected, these gaps could be used by Sponsor to assert that undocumented instructions or conduct modified Quintiles' obligations, exposing Quintiles to uncompensated scope creep and disputed budget adjustments.
suggestions.original_text: Change Orders. Any change in the details of a Work Order or the assumptions upon which the Work Order is based (including, but not limited to, changes in an agreed starting date for a Project or suspension of the Project by Sponsor) may require changes in the budget and/or timelines, and shall require a written amendment to the Work Order (a “Change Order”). Each Change Order shall detail the requested changes to the applicable task, responsibility, duty, budget, timeline or other matter. The Change Order will become effective upon the execution of the Change Order by both parties, and the parties will agree upon a reasonable period of time within which Quintiles shall implement the changes. Both parties agree to act in good faith and promptly when considering a Change Order requested by the other party. Without limiting the foregoing, Sponsor agrees that it will not unreasonably withhold approval of a Change Order, if the proposed changes in budgets or timelines result from, among other appropriate reasons, forces outside the reasonable control of Quintiles or Sponsor’s changes in the assumptions upon which the initial budget or timelines were based, including, but not limited to, the assumptions set forth in the budget or timelines. Quintiles reserves the right to postpone effecting material changes in the Project’s scope until such time as the parties agree to and execute the corresponding Change Order. For any Change Order that affects the scope of the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles, Quintiles and Sponsor shall execute a corresponding amendment to the Transfer of Obligations Form. Sponsor shall file such amendment where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Change Orders. Any change in the details of a Work Order or the assumptions upon which the Work Order is based (including, but not limited to, changes in an agreed starting date for a Project or suspension of the Project by Sponsor) may require changes in the budget and/or timelines, and shall require a written amendment to the Work Order (a "Change Order"). No amendment to this Agreement, any Work Order, or any schedule or exhibit hereto shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument signed by duly authorized representatives of both parties. Each Change Order shall detail the requested changes to the applicable task, responsibility, duty, budget, timeline or other matter. The Change Order will become effective upon the execution of the Change Order by duly authorized representatives of both parties, and the parties will agree upon a reasonable period of time within which Quintiles shall implement the changes. No oral agreement, course of conduct, or course of dealing between the parties shall constitute or be deemed to constitute an amendment to this Agreement, any Work Order, or any Change Order. Both parties agree to act in good faith and promptly when considering a Change Order requested by the other party. Without limiting the foregoing, Sponsor agrees that it will not unreasonably withhold approval of a Change Order, if the proposed changes in budgets or timelines result from, among other appropriate reasons, forces outside the reasonable control of Quintiles or Sponsor's changes in the assumptions upon which the initial budget or timelines were based, including, but not limited to, the assumptions set forth in the budget or timelines. Quintiles reserves the right to postpone effecting material changes in the Project's scope until such time as the parties agree to and execute the corresponding Change Order. For any Change Order that affects the scope of the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles, Quintiles and Sponsor shall execute a corresponding amendment to the Transfer of Obligations Form. Sponsor shall file such amendment where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.

suggestions.reason: The clause captures all data and information made known to Quintiles as a result of Services—with no marking, designation, or reasonable-person identification test—exposing Quintiles, Inc. to a claim that virtually any communication from Sponsor constitutes Sponsor Confidential Information, regardless of whether it was reasonably understood to be confidential at the time. More critically, the clause is entirely one-sided: it confers confidentiality protection exclusively on Sponsor's information while affording Quintiles, Inc. no corresponding contractual protection for its own proprietary methodologies, tools, processes, and business information that Quintiles discloses to Sponsor in the course of performing the Services. Left unaddressed, Quintiles, Inc. would bear significant, open-ended confidentiality obligations while remaining commercially exposed with no equivalent safeguard for its own sensitive information.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter “Sponsor Confidential Information”) written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, each party and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to the other party. All such data and information ("Confidential Information") written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to the receiving party and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement, that is designated as confidential at the time of disclosure or that by its nature or the circumstances of disclosure would reasonably be understood to be confidential, shall be considered confidential and shall remain the sole property of the disclosing party.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Quintiles, Inc. to three material gaps: it imposes no standard of care on the receiving party for protecting Confidential Information, meaning Sponsor faces no enforceable benchmark if it handles Quintiles' proprietary data carelessly; it restricts disclosure to a need-to-know basis but does not require that recipients be bound by written confidentiality obligations, leaving Quintiles' Confidential Information unprotected once shared with Sponsor's personnel or contractors; and it contains no obligation to return or destroy Quintiles' Confidential Information upon request or at termination, allowing Sponsor to retain Quintiles' information indefinitely. These omissions collectively undermine the enforceability of Quintiles, Inc.'s confidentiality protections under this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked ‘confidential’, or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party’s obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period often (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked 'confidential', or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information on a need-to-know basis, to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement, and only to those employees, contractors, or agents who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party's obligations hereunder, and each party shall protect the other party's Confidential Information using at least the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, but in no event less than reasonable care. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period of ten (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.

suggestions.clause: Ownership and Inventions; No Implied Rights
suggestions.reason: The "Sponsor's Property" provision vests ownership in Sponsor but is entirely silent on what happens if the materials, documents, programs, or information that Sponsor supplies to Quintiles infringe a third party's intellectual property rights. This exposes Quintiles to unindemnified third-party infringement claims arising solely from its use of Sponsor-supplied materials in performing services under this Agreement, with no contractual recourse against Sponsor. Without an express representation by Sponsor and a corresponding responsibility allocation, Quintiles bears the financial and reputational risk of claims it had no ability to prevent. If a separate indemnification provision exists elsewhere in the Agreement, it should be confirmed to extend to third-party IP infringement claims arising from Sponsor's Property.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor’s Property. Sponsor’s property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively “Sponsor’s Property”).
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor's Property. Sponsor's property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively "Sponsor's Property"). Sponsor represents that, to the best of Sponsor's knowledge, Sponsor's Property does not infringe any third party's intellectual property rights, and Sponsor shall be responsible for any third-party claims arising out of Quintiles' use of Sponsor's Property as directed under this Agreement.

suggestions.clause: Ownership and Inventions; No Implied Rights
suggestions.reason: The license granted to Sponsor over Quintiles' Software lacks an express purpose restriction: as drafted, Sponsor's right to use "in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement" is broader than the narrow functional trigger that justifies the license (i.e., accessing, retrieving, or using the study data generated by Quintiles' Services). Without a "solely for the purpose of" limitation mirroring that trigger, Quintiles, Inc. faces a material risk that Sponsor could use the licensed software—and any improvements thereto—for activities unrelated to that specific study data access need, undermining the proprietary value of Quintiles' IP. This gap is commercially significant given that the clause simultaneously designates Quintiles' Property as Quintiles Confidential Information, creating an internal inconsistency if the license scope is construed more broadly than the confidentiality designation intends.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles’ Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor’s Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs, is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles’ Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles' Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor's Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs) is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right of use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties), without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto, solely for the purpose of accessing, retrieving, or using such study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement in connection with such Sponsor project. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles' Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.

suggestions.reason: The Records and Materials clause, as drafted, imposes record-keeping and delivery obligations exclusively on Quintiles while conferring no defined audit right on either party, leaving Quintiles exposed to open-ended, unscheduled inspections at Sponsor's initiative with no agreed scope, frequency cap, advance notice requirement, or cost allocation. Without these parameters, Quintiles faces the operational and financial risk of unlimited, disruptive audits with no obligation on Sponsor to bear the associated costs, and no obligation to confine its inspection to relevant records, systems, or premises. Additionally, the absence of a defined retention period ties Quintiles to an indefinite and potentially costly record-keeping obligation, and the lack of any requirement for Sponsor to identify and allow remediation of audit findings exposes Quintiles to unresolved compliance assertions. Counsel for Quintiles should also confirm that the survival clause in the Agreement expressly covers this provision, as record-keeping and audit obligations must remain enforceable after termination or expiry.
suggestions.original_text: Records and Materials. Quintiles agrees to retain all records and data generated in the performance of any Project under this Agreement, and other Project-related materials including without limitation Sponsor’s proprietary compound (“Records and Materials”), and further agrees to maintain all Records and Materials in a secure area reasonably protected from fire, theft and destruction. At the completion of the Services by Quintiles, all materials, information and all other data owned by Sponsor, regardless of the method of storage or retrieval, shall be delivered to Sponsor in such form as is then currently in the possession of Quintiles, subject to the payment obligations set forth in Section 2 herein. Alternatively, at Sponsor’s option and written request, such materials and data may be (i) retained by Quintiles for Sponsor for an agreed-upon time period, or (ii) disposed of pursuant to the written directions of Sponsor. Sponsor shall pay the costs associated with any of the above options and shall pay a to-be-determined fee for storage by Quintiles of records and materials after completion or termination of the Services. Quintiles, however, reserves the right to retain, at its own cost and subject to the confidentiality provisions herein, copies of all materials that may be needed to satisfy regulatory requirements or to resolve disputes regarding the Services. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer from Sponsor to Quintiles any FDA or regulatory record-keeping requirements unless such transfer is specifically provided for in the applicable Transfer of Obligations Form.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Records and Materials. Quintiles agrees to retain all records and data generated in the performance of any Project under this Agreement, and other Project-related materials including without limitation Sponsor's proprietary compound ("Records and Materials"), for the period required by applicable law and regulatory requirements, and further agrees to maintain all Records and Materials in a secure area reasonably protected from fire, theft and destruction. Sponsor shall have the right, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice and no more than once per calendar year, to audit or inspect Quintiles' relevant records, systems, and premises solely to verify Quintiles' compliance with this Agreement. Quintiles shall cooperate reasonably with any such audit and shall provide access to relevant Records and Materials and personnel. The costs of any such audit shall be borne by Sponsor, except where an audit reveals a material breach by Quintiles, in which case Quintiles shall bear the reasonable documented costs of that audit. Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with a written summary of any material findings, and Quintiles shall have thirty (30) days following receipt to correct any confirmed deficiency. At the completion of the Services by Quintiles, all materials, information and all other data owned by Sponsor, regardless of the method of storage or retrieval, shall be delivered to Sponsor in such form as is then currently in the possession of Quintiles, subject to the payment obligations set forth in Section 2 herein. Alternatively, at Sponsor's option and written request, such materials and data may be (i) retained by Quintiles for Sponsor for an agreed-upon time period, or (ii) disposed of pursuant to the written directions of Sponsor. Sponsor shall pay the costs associated with any of the above options and shall pay a to-be-determined fee for storage by Quintiles of records and materials after completion or termination of the Services. Quintiles, however, reserves the right to retain, at its own cost and subject to the confidentiality provisions herein, copies of all materials that may be needed to satisfy regulatory requirements or to resolve disputes regarding the Services. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to transfer from Sponsor to Quintiles any FDA or regulatory record-keeping requirements unless such transfer is specifically provided for in the applicable Transfer of Obligations Form.

suggestions.reason: The clause correctly disclaims a partnership, agency, employment, and joint venture relationship but omits two elements that are material to Quintiles, Inc.'s risk exposure: a statement confirming that each party controls the manner and means by which its own personnel perform work, and a clear allocation of responsibility for personnel compensation, taxes, and benefits. Without these elements, the clause provides an incomplete basis for defending against a worker-misclassification claim or a tax-authority challenge, either of which could result in Quintiles, Inc. being held liable for the counterparty's payroll taxes, benefit obligations, or employment-law claims. The absence of a control-of-performance statement also weakens Quintiles, Inc.'s ability to demonstrate the operational independence that is central to a legitimate independent contractor classification.
suggestions.original_text: Independent Contractor Relationship. For the purposes of this Agreement, the parties hereto are independent contractors and nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to place them in the relationship of partners, principal and agent, employer/employee or joint venturers. Neither party shall have the power or right to bind or obligate the other party, and neither party shall hold itself out as having such authority.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Independent Contractor Relationship. For the purposes of this Agreement, the parties hereto are independent contractors and nothing contained in this Agreement shall be construed to place them in the relationship of partners, principal and agent, employer/employee or joint venturers. Each party shall retain sole control over the manner and means by which its personnel perform work under this Agreement, and each party shall be solely responsible for all compensation, taxes, and benefits of its own personnel. Neither party shall have the power or right to bind or obligate the other party, and neither party shall hold itself out as having such authority.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Quintiles, Inc. to three material compliance gaps. First, the absence of any anti-bribery and anti-corruption commitment leaves Quintiles without a contractual anchor if Sponsor-directed activities implicate applicable anti-corruption laws, creating regulatory liability risk for Quintiles as the performing party. Second, neither party is obligated to notify the other of a law or policy breach affecting the Agreement, meaning Quintiles could remain uninformed of a Sponsor-side compliance failure that directly impacts the Services or triggers downstream regulatory or reputational exposure for Quintiles. Third, the clause contains no supply-chain due-diligence standard addressing forced labour, child labour, or human trafficking, which increasingly represents a legal and reputational risk for contract research organizations operating across multi-jurisdiction supply chains.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing if it becomes aware of any breach of applicable law or regulation that materially affects the performance of or compliance with this Agreement. Regarding the FDA's electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 ("Part 11"), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles' standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Each party further represents that it maintains reasonable policies and procedures designed to address forced labour, child labour, and human trafficking in its supply chain. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause imposes a unilateral representation and an ongoing forward-looking covenant exclusively on Quintiles, Inc., with no corresponding obligation on Sponsor, exposing Quintiles, Inc. to unbalanced contractual risk and potential claims without any reciprocal commitment from the counterparty. The phrase "in any way prevent" is impermissibly broad and undefined: a court could read it to capture incidental scheduling overlaps or partial resource allocation issues that do not meaningfully impair delivery of the Services, creating a standard Quintiles, Inc. could inadvertently breach through ordinary business activities. This overbreadth, combined with the absence of a materiality threshold, creates unlimited exposure for Quintiles, Inc. — including potential claims for breach of representation or warranty — without any cap or fault-based limitation. The initial conflict-of-agreement representation should also bind Sponsor on a mutual basis, as Sponsor's own pre-existing or future commitments could equally impair performance of its obligations under this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Conflict of Agreements. Quintiles represents to Sponsor that it is not a party to any agreement which would prevent it from fulfilling its obligations under this Agreement and that during the term of this Agreement, Quintiles agrees that it will not enter into any agreement to provide services which would in any way prevent it from providing the Services contemplated under this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Conflict of Agreements. Each party represents to the other that it is not a party to any agreement which would prevent it from fulfilling its obligations under this Agreement and that during the term of this Agreement, Quintiles agrees that it will not enter into any agreement to provide services which would materially prevent it from providing the Services contemplated under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The opening sentence restricts only Quintiles and its affiliates from publishing or referring to project data, while imposing no reciprocal constraint on Sponsor, exposing Quintiles to a unilateral approval regime that Sponsor itself need not observe. As a contract research organization, Quintiles also faces regulatory and legal obligations that may compel disclosure of project data, and the absence of any carve-out for legally required disclosures places Quintiles at risk of a consent-breach claim merely for complying with applicable law or regulation. Additionally, the name-use restriction in the second sentence covers only "name" and does not extend to logos or trademarks, leaving Quintiles without contractual protection against unauthorized use of its broader brand assets.
suggestions.original_text: Publication; Use of Name. Project data or results may not be published or referred to, in whole or in part, by Quintiles or its affiliates without the prior expressed written consent of Sponsor. Neither party will use the other party’s name in connection with any publication or promotion without the other party’s prior, written consent.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Publication; Use of Name. Project data or results may not be published or referred to, in whole or in part, by either party or its affiliates without the prior written consent of the other party, except to the extent required by applicable law or regulation. Neither party will use the other party's name, logo, or trademarks in connection with any publication or promotion without the other party's prior, written consent.

suggestions.reason: The exclusion of consequential and indirect losses in the first paragraph is drafted solely to protect Quintiles and its affiliates, with no corresponding restriction on Sponsor's ability to pursue those same categories of loss against Quintiles. This asymmetry creates a material enforceability risk for Quintiles, Inc.: a court may treat the one-sided exclusion as an unreasonable or unconscionable term and strike it in its entirety, leaving Quintiles fully exposed to uncapped claims for lost profits, lost goodwill, and special or consequential damages by Sponsor. Making the exclusion mutual preserves the commercial intent of the limitation while substantially improving its defensibility and enforceability across all theories of liability.
suggestions.original_text: Limitation of Liability. Neither Quintiles, nor its affiliates, nor any of Quintiles’ or its affiliate’s directors, officers, employees, subcontractors or agents shall have any liability of any type (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence, and tort liability), for any loss of profits, opportunity or goodwill, or any type of special, incidental, indirect or consequential damage or loss in connection with or arising out of this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services performed by Quintiles hereunder. In addition, in no event shall the collective, aggregate liability (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence and tort liability) of Quintiles or its affiliates, or Quintiles’ or its affiliates’ directors, officers, employees, subcontractors and agents, under this Agreement or any Work Order hereunder exceed the amount of fees actually received by Quintiles from Sponsor for the assignment or task from which such liability arose.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Limitation of Liability. Neither party, nor its affiliates, nor any of its or its affiliates' directors, officers, employees, subcontractors or agents shall have any liability of any type (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence, and tort liability), for any loss of profits, opportunity or goodwill, or any type of special, incidental, indirect or consequential damage or loss in connection with or arising out of this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services performed by Quintiles hereunder. In addition, in no event shall the collective, aggregate liability (including, but not limited to, contract, negligence and tort liability) of Quintiles or its affiliates, or Quintiles' or its affiliates' directors, officers, employees, subcontractors and agents, under this Agreement or any Work Order hereunder exceed the amount of fees actually received by Quintiles from Sponsor for the assignment or task from which such liability arose.

suggestions.reason: The limitation of liability framework in this Agreement is structurally one-sided: the aggregate liability cap expressly references only Quintiles and its affiliates, leaving Sponsor without a reciprocal cap and exposing Quintiles to unlimited claims from an uncapped counterparty. More critically, the clause contains no express carve-outs preserving uncapped liability for fraud or wilful misconduct, nor does it address whether the cap governs data breach, confidentiality breach, IP infringement, or indemnification obligations—categories where courts may decline to enforce contractual caps and where Quintiles faces its most significant exposure in a clinical research services context. Without these protections, Quintiles cannot accurately quantify or cap its financial risk across the Agreement's highest-value risk categories.
suggestions.original_text: EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATION OR WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, ANY WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT OF A PATENT, TRADEMARK OR OTHER INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHT.
suggestions.suggested_fix: EXCEPT AS OTHERWISE SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT, NEITHER PARTY MAKES ANY REPRESENTATION OR WARRANTY, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING, WITHOUT LIMITATION, ANY WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE OR NON-INFRINGEMENT OF A PATENT, TRADEMARK OR OTHER INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHT. ALL LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL APPLY MUTUALLY TO BOTH PARTIES AND SHALL NOT LIMIT EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY FOR FRAUD, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT, DEATH OR PERSONAL INJURY CAUSED BY NEGLIGENCE, BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS, DATA BREACH, INFRINGEMENT OF INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS, OR INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the indemnification clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to material financial risk on four grounds: (i) Quintiles' reciprocal indemnity omits the "defend" obligation and lacks the "solely" fault qualifier that limits Sponsor's indemnity exposure, creating an asymmetric standard that could be used against Quintiles; (ii) the clause contains no claims-handling mechanics, meaning Sponsor could argue that Quintiles' failure to provide timely notice or tender control of the defense prejudices or extinguishes its indemnification rights; (iii) there is no express statement that indemnification obligations are carved out from any limitation of liability, leaving open a counterparty argument that Sponsor's indemnity payments to Quintiles are capped by the Agreement's liability ceiling; and (iv) the absence of a mitigation obligation on the indemnified party may cause a court to imply a stricter standard or undermine the enforceability of the clause in certain jurisdictions.
suggestions.original_text: Indemnification. Sponsor shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Quintiles and its affiliates, and its and their directors, officers, employees and agents (each, a “Quintiles Indemnified Party”), from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, reasonable attorney fees, court costs, and expenses (collectively “Losses”), joint or several, resulting or arising from any third-party claims, actions, proceedings, investigations or litigation relating to or arising from or in connection with this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services contemplated herein (including, without limitation, any Losses arising from or in connection with any study, test, device, product or potential product to which this Agreement or any Work Order relates), except to the extent such Losses are determined to have resulted solely from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party seeking indemnity hereunder. Quintiles shall indemnify and hold harmless Sponsor, its affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees and agents harmless from and against any Losses arising from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Indemnification. Sponsor shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Quintiles and its affiliates, and its and their directors, officers, employees and agents (each, a "Quintiles Indemnified Party"), from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, reasonable attorney fees, court costs, and expenses (collectively "Losses"), joint or several, resulting or arising from any third-party claims, actions, proceedings, investigations or litigation relating to or arising from or in connection with this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services contemplated herein (including, without limitation, any Losses arising from or in connection with any study, test, device, product or potential product to which this Agreement or any Work Order relates), except to the extent such Losses are determined to have resulted solely from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party seeking indemnity hereunder. Quintiles shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sponsor, its affiliates and their respective directors, officers, employees and agents from and against any Losses arising solely from the negligence or intentional misconduct of a Quintiles Indemnified Party. The party seeking indemnification shall provide the indemnifying party with prompt written notice of any claim, shall grant the indemnifying party control of the defense and settlement of such claim (provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or admission of liability on the indemnified party shall be made without such party's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld), and shall provide reasonable cooperation in connection with such defense, at the indemnifying party's cost. Each indemnified party shall take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate any Losses for which indemnification is sought hereunder. The indemnification obligations set forth in this Section shall not be subject to any limitation of liability set forth elsewhere in this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to significant indemnification risk on multiple fronts: it fails to identify what events actually trigger indemnity (such as third-party claims, IP infringement, or breach of law), does not define which party owes the obligation to which, and omits the scope of recoverable losses such as damages, costs, and attorneys' fees—leaving Quintiles unable to enforce or quantify any indemnity right it may hold. The absence of a mitigation obligation on the indemnified party, combined with the lack of any carve-out from or subordination to the Agreement's limitation of liability provisions, means Quintiles could face uncapped indemnification exposure with no corresponding procedural protection. If this clause is read as the entirety of the indemnification regime, the indemnification obligations should also be reviewed for alignment with any limitation of liability provision elsewhere in the Agreement to confirm they are not inadvertently capped.
suggestions.original_text: Indemnification Procedure. Any party seeking indemnity hereunder shall (a) give prompt notice to the other party (the “Indemnifying Party”) of any such claim or lawsuit (including a copy thereof) served upon it, (b) permit the Indemnifying Party to assume full responsibility to investigate, prepare for, and defend against such claim or lawsuit, (c) shall fully cooperate with the Indemnifying Party and its legal representatives in the investigation of any matter the subject of indemnification, and (d) shall not compromise or settle such claim or lawsuit in a manner that adversely affects the other party’s rights under this Agreement without the Indemnifying Party’s prior written consent. The party seeking indemnity shall not unreasonably withhold its approval of the settlement of any claim, liability, or action covered by this Indemnification provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Indemnification Procedure. Each party (the "Indemnifying Party") shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party (the "Indemnified Party") from and against any third-party claims, damages, losses, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from the Indemnifying Party's breach of this Agreement, negligence, willful misconduct, or infringement of any third-party intellectual property right. Such indemnification obligations shall not be subject to any limitation of liability set forth in this Agreement. The Indemnified Party shall (a) give prompt notice to the Indemnifying Party of any such claim or lawsuit (including a copy thereof) served upon it, (b) permit the Indemnifying Party to assume full responsibility to investigate, prepare for, and defend against such claim or lawsuit, (c) fully cooperate with the Indemnifying Party and its legal representatives in the investigation of any matter the subject of indemnification, and (d) not compromise or settle such claim or lawsuit without the Indemnifying Party's prior written consent. The Indemnified Party shall take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate its losses and shall not unreasonably withhold its approval of the settlement of any claim, liability, or action covered by this Indemnification provision.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, only Sponsor holds a unilateral right to terminate without cause, leaving Quintiles, Inc. with no equivalent exit right and no mechanism to wind down its own obligations on commercially reasonable terms. The absence of any transition assistance framework—covering scope, duration, applicable fees, and cooperation with a replacement provider—means Quintiles, Inc. could be compelled to perform complex handover activities at its own cost with no contractual protection. Without a survival clause, Quintiles, Inc.'s rights to accrued payment, confidentiality protections, indemnification, and limitation of liability are unenforceable once the Agreement terminates, creating significant financial and legal exposure. These gaps collectively leave Quintiles, Inc. in an operationally and financially vulnerable position on exit.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) day’s prior written notice to Quintiles.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party. Upon expiration or termination, Sponsor shall pay Quintiles for all Services performed and non-cancellable commitments incurred through the effective termination date. Quintiles shall provide reasonable transition assistance, including data return and knowledge transfer, for up to ninety (90) days following the effective termination date, at its then-current rates and charged to Sponsor. Sponsor shall cooperate with and facilitate Quintiles' handover to any replacement provider. Provisions relating to payment obligations, confidentiality, indemnification, intellectual property, and limitation of liability shall survive termination or expiration of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause requires only a "close-out schedule" following expiry of the cure period, without mandating a formal transition plan that addresses the handover of work product, data, and ongoing study activities to the counterparty or its designee. For Quintiles, Inc., as a contract research organization performing complex, ongoing clinical services, this gap creates material operational and financial exposure: Quintiles could be required to wind down and hand over active work streams with no defined scope, structure, or compensation framework for transition assistance, leaving it vulnerable to open-ended post-termination obligations and disputes over what constitutes necessary close-out work. Without an express right to compensation for Services and transition assistance performed during the close-out period, Quintiles, Inc. risks performing substantial wind-down work without recovery at applicable Work Order rates.
suggestions.original_text: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days’ written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days' written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule and transition plan, which shall address the orderly handover of work product, data, and ongoing activities to the counterparty or its designee, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations. Quintiles shall be compensated at the rates set forth in the applicable Work Order for all Services and transition assistance performed during the close-out period.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes close-out obligations on Quintiles upon receipt of a termination notice but is entirely silent on transition assistance, creating a material gap that exposes Quintiles, Inc. to a significant risk: the counterparty could demand that Quintiles assist in migrating work, data, or regulatory submissions to a successor provider with no contractual entitlement for Quintiles to be compensated for that effort. Without an express provision tying any such transition assistance to payment at applicable Work Order rates, the counterparty could argue that transition obligations are subsumed within the existing close-out duties, leaving Quintiles, Inc. absorbing the cost of substantial uncompensated post-termination resource deployment. Adding a compensation-linked transition assistance sentence protects Quintiles, Inc.'s financial position and aligns with standard market practice for clinical and professional services agreements.
suggestions.original_text: Upon receipt of a termination notice, Quintiles shall promptly cease performing any work not necessary for the orderly close out of the affected Project(s), or for the fulfillment of any regulatory requirements, and will submit an itemized accounting of the Services completed, expenses incurred pursuant to the performance of the Services, any non-cancelable expenses incurred relating to the unfinished Work Order, and payments received in order to determine a balance to be paid by either party to the other. Such balance will be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt of such itemized accounting.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon receipt of a termination notice, Quintiles shall promptly cease performing any work not necessary for the orderly close out of the affected Project(s), or for the fulfillment of any regulatory requirements, and will submit an itemized accounting of the Services completed, expenses incurred pursuant to the performance of the Services, any non-cancelable expenses incurred relating to the unfinished Work Order, and payments received in order to determine a balance to be paid by either party to the other. Such balance will be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt of such itemized accounting. Upon written request, Quintiles shall provide reasonable transition assistance following the effective date of termination to facilitate the orderly handover of affected Project(s) to the counterparty or its designee, and the counterparty shall compensate Quintiles for all such transition assistance at the rates applicable under the relevant Work Order.

suggestions.reason: When a Sponsor affiliate executes a Work Order directly and uses Quintiles' services, that affiliate receives all rights and protections afforded to Sponsor, yet the clause imposes no corresponding obligation on Sponsor to guarantee or remain liable for its affiliate's payment and performance obligations. This creates a material financial risk for Quintiles, Inc.: if a Sponsor affiliate defaults on fees or other obligations under a Work Order, Quintiles' recourse is limited solely to the affiliate entity, which may lack the creditworthiness or assets of Sponsor itself. Without an express Sponsor guarantee or joint and several liability, Quintiles, Inc. is effectively extending services and credit to unvetted affiliate entities with no contractual backstop from the Sponsor that entered into this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor’s affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor’s affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term “affiliate” shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term “control” shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity.

Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly.
