suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the subcontracting regime exposes Quintiles, Inc. to three compounding risks: Sponsor may withhold or delay approval arbitrarily, as there is no reasonableness standard governing that consent, which could paralyze Quintiles' ability to perform its Project obligations; the phrase "sufficient information to enable proper evaluation" is undefined and subjective, leaving Sponsor free to demand open-ended disclosure or to dispute whether any submission was adequate; and the unqualified retention of "any of its obligations" in condition (ii) renders Quintiles fully and potentially unlimitedly liable for a subcontractor's defaults without reference to the Agreement's existing limitation of liability provisions, creating a gap that could be exploited to circumvent agreed liability caps. Left unaddressed, these terms would give Sponsor broad, unilateral leverage over Quintiles' operational and contractual performance while simultaneously exposing Quintiles to uncapped financial liability for acts it does not directly control.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, including providing Sponsor with sufficient information to enable proper evaluation of such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0,6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles shall have the right to subcontract a portion of its obligations in connection with its performance of any Project (other than to its corporate affiliates), provided that (i) Quintiles shall have obtained the prior written approval of Sponsor to the subcontract, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, including providing Sponsor with information reasonably necessary to evaluate such subcontractor; (ii) such subcontract shall not relieve Quintiles of any of its obligations under this Agreement, subject to the limitation of liability provisions of this Agreement; (iii) Quintiles shall enter into a written agreement with each subcontractor on terms and conditions consistent with this Agreement, including for the benefit of Sponsor, provisions substantially similar to those of Sections 5.0, 6.0, and 11.0; (iv) each Work Order, when appropriate, shall specify the name of such subcontractors; and (v) if requested by Sponsor, Quintiles agrees to provide Sponsor with a copy of each such subcontract.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "in a timely manner" governing Sponsor's obligation to forward documents and materials to Quintiles is commercially unenforceable as a time standard because it creates no objectively measurable deadline against which Quintiles can assess Sponsor's performance or trigger the breach protection in sentence three. Without a definite timeframe, Sponsor may dispute whether its delivery was "timely," effectively undermining Quintiles' shield from liability for errors, delays, or consequences arising from Sponsor's failure to cooperate. This ambiguity exposes Quintiles, Inc. to the risk of bearing financial and operational responsibility for downstream performance failures that are directly attributable to Sponsor's delayed cooperation, since the absence of a fixed deadline makes it difficult for Quintiles to demonstrate the causal link required to invoke the exculpatory provision. The obligation should be anchored to a specific period following Quintiles' written request to give that protection meaningful force.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor’s possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor’s failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles within [__] Business Days following Quintiles' written request therefor all documents, materials and information in Sponsor's possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor's failure to provide documents, materials or information within the period required under this Section or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.

suggestions.reason: The obligation to notify "immediately" imposes a strict but undefined temporal standard on Quintiles, Inc., exposing it to a breach claim from Sponsor the moment any notification is characterised as delayed — without a clear trigger anchoring when the clock starts running. Additionally, the requirement to use "good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution" is an indefinite and subjective standard that could bind Quintiles, Inc. to protracted negotiations without an objectively measurable endpoint, creating litigation risk over whether Quintiles, Inc. discharged that obligation. Replacing "immediately" with "promptly upon becoming aware" clarifies the trigger event and protects Quintiles, Inc. from constructive-knowledge arguments, while substituting "commercially reasonable efforts" for "good faith efforts" anchors the negotiation obligation to an objective, enforceable standard under applicable US law.
suggestions.original_text: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing promptly upon becoming aware of any material delays or limits encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Quintiles' compliance obligation extends not only to applicable laws, rules, and regulations but also to any "written instructions provided by Sponsor" relating to storage and handling, without any reasonableness qualifier. This grants Sponsor an unchecked unilateral power to expand Quintiles' operational obligations at will—potentially imposing instructions that are commercially impracticable, inconsistent with Quintiles' own regulatory requirements, or operationally disruptive—and Quintiles would be in breach if it failed to follow them. The absence of a reasonableness standard creates material legal and financial exposure for Quintiles, since any deviation from even an arbitrary or burdensome Sponsor instruction could be characterised as a default under this Agreement. Qualifying Sponsor's written instructions as "reasonable" is the minimum market-standard protection necessary to shield Quintiles from open-ended, unilaterally imposed compliance obligations.
suggestions.original_text: Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including reasonable written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the Force Majeure clause creates significant operational and financial risk for Quintiles, Inc. because it contains no notice requirement, no obligation on the affected party to mitigate or resume performance, and no right for Quintiles, Inc. to terminate if a prolonged force majeure event renders the counterparty's performance indefinitely suspended. The clause also fails to carve out events within a party's own control or caused by its own acts or omissions—meaning a counterparty could invoke force majeure to excuse failures attributable to its own supplier mismanagement or preventable internal labor disputes. Without a stated termination right triggered by a continued delay, Quintiles, Inc. could be left bound to an Agreement with no recourse if the counterparty remains non-performing for an indefinite period, and without a continuity obligations carve-out, critical recovery commitments could similarly be suspended.
suggestions.original_text: Force Majeure. In the event either party shall be delayed or hindered in or prevented from the performance of any act required hereunder by reasons of strike, lockouts, labor troubles, inability to procure materials or services, failure of power or restrictive government or judicial orders, or decrees, riots, insurrection, war, Acts of God, inclement weather or other reason or cause beyond that party’s control, then performance of such act (except for the payment of money owed) shall be excused for the period of such delay.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Force Majeure. In the event either party shall be delayed or hindered in or prevented from the performance of any act required hereunder by reasons of strike, lockouts, labor troubles, inability to procure materials or services, failure of power or restrictive government or judicial orders, or decrees, riots, insurrection, war, Acts of God, inclement weather, or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control and not caused or contributed to by that party's own acts or omissions, then performance of such act (except for the payment of money owed) shall be excused for the period of such delay, provided that: (i) the affected party promptly notifies the other party in writing of the event and its anticipated duration; (ii) the affected party uses commercially reasonable efforts to limit the effect of such delay and to resume full performance; and (iii) any applicable continuity or recovery obligations of the affected party shall remain in effect during such delay. If such delay continues for more than thirty (30) days, the non-affected party may terminate the affected obligations upon written notice to the other party.

suggestions.reason: The notice block for Quintiles, Inc. contains no mechanism by which Quintiles may update its designated contact or address, meaning that notices directed to a departed officer or a superseded address could be deemed validly delivered against Quintiles even where Quintiles had no actual receipt. This creates a concrete operational risk for Quintiles, Inc.: personnel changes, office relocations, or a change in the responsible General Manager could leave Quintiles unable to receive time-sensitive legal notices—such as termination notices or indemnity claims—without any contractual remedy. A standard change-of-notice provision is the market-accepted cure and should be inserted to protect Quintiles, Inc.'s ability to control its own notice details throughout the term of the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: If to Quintiles: Quintiles, Inc., 10245 Hickman Mills Drive, Kansas City, MO 64137, Attn: Michael J. Baltezor, Ph.D., General Manager
suggestions.suggested_fix: If to Quintiles: Quintiles, Inc., 10245 Hickman Mills Drive, Kansas City, MO 64137, Attn: Michael J. Baltezor, Ph.D., General Manager, or to such other address or addressee as Quintiles, Inc. may designate by written notice to the other party.

suggestions.reason: The clause restricts required coverage to "during the term of this Agreement" only, which creates a material gap for Quintiles, Inc. because Professional Liability policies are typically written on a claims-made basis, meaning that claims filed after expiration or termination—arising from services performed during the term—may be uninsured unless a post-term tail period is expressly required. Additionally, General Liability under item 2) is not expressly assigned to both parties, leaving it ambiguous as to whether Sponsor must also carry it, which weakens Quintiles, Inc.'s ability to enforce minimum coverage against Sponsor. Most critically, the absence of any statement that the stated insurance minimums do not cap or limit either party's liability exposes Quintiles, Inc. to the argument that its remedies against Sponsor are constrained by those policy thresholds.
suggestions.original_text: Insurance. During the term of this Agreement to cover its obligations hereunder, each party shall maintain insurance coverage as follows: 1) (a) Professional Liability for Quintiles in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; (b) Product Liability for Sponsor in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; and 2) General Liability in amounts of at least US$3,000,000.00. All insurance amounts may be obtained by full, individual primary policy amount; a primary amount of less than minimum requirement enhanced by a blanket excess umbrella policy; or a combination of either. Each party shall provide the other party with a certificate of insurance upon request. The insured shall provide the other party with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of any material change, cancellation or expiration of the above-required insurance.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Insurance. During the term of this Agreement and for a period of not less than three (3) years following expiration or termination of this Agreement, to cover its obligations hereunder, each party shall maintain insurance coverage as follows: 1) (a) Professional Liability for Quintiles in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; (b) Product Liability for Sponsor in an amount of at least US$10,000,000.00; and 2) General Liability for each party in amounts of at least US$3,000,000.00. All insurance amounts may be obtained by full, individual primary policy amount; a primary amount of less than minimum requirement enhanced by a blanket excess umbrella policy; or a combination of either. The minimum insurance amounts set forth in this Section shall not be construed to limit or cap either party's liability under this Agreement. Each party shall provide the other party with a certificate of insurance upon request. The insured shall provide the other party with at least thirty (30) days prior written notice of any material change, cancellation or expiration of the above-required insurance.

suggestions.reason: The final sentence of this clause obliges the parties to include "a currency exchange provision" in qualifying Work Orders but specifies no minimum content for that provision, creating an unenforceable agreement to agree that exposes Quintiles, Inc. to unquantified foreign exchange risk if the parties dispute or fail to negotiate the terms of such a provision. Without a defined methodology or a contractual fallback, Quintiles, Inc. has no self-executing remedy and could bear the full cost of adverse currency movements on Work Orders exceeding $500,000. The absence of a default mechanism also means that a Sponsor could resist inclusion of a commercially adequate provision in a Work Order, leaving Quintiles, Inc. with no contractual basis to convert and recover fees at an objective rate. This gap is material given that the pass-through cost mechanism in the same clause already references an objective Oanda rate benchmark that could serve as an appropriate default.
suggestions.original_text: Foreign Currency Exchange. The currency to be used for invoice and payment shall be the currency stated in the Budget or Table attached to the Work Order (the “Contracted Currency”). If Quintiles incurs pass-through costs in a currency other than the Contracted Currency, then Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for Quintiles’ actual costs in the Contracted Currency based on the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate (Oanda.com) for the applicable currencies on the last business Friday of the month. For Work Orders that involve the performance of Services by Quintiles or its affiliates in any countries that use currencies other than the Contracted Currency, and the fees for such Services will exceed $500,000, then a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Foreign Currency Exchange. The currency to be used for invoice and payment shall be the currency stated in the Budget or Table attached to the Work Order (the "Contracted Currency"). If Quintiles incurs pass-through costs in a currency other than the Contracted Currency, then Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for Quintiles' actual costs in the Contracted Currency based on the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate (Oanda.com) for the applicable currencies on the last business Friday of the month. For Work Orders that involve the performance of Services by Quintiles or its affiliates in any countries that use currencies other than the Contracted Currency, and the fees for such Services will exceed $500,000, then a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order, which provision shall at minimum specify the applicable exchange rate methodology and the applicable currency conversion date; provided that if no such provision is included in the Work Order, the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate (Oanda.com) on the last business Friday of the applicable month shall apply by default.

suggestions.reason: The clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to enforcement risk on two related fronts: first, the phrase "at the beginning of each calendar year" does not specify an effective date or require advance notice, leaving the counterparty room to dispute whether a fee increase was properly and timely invoked, potentially defeating Quintiles' ability to collect the adjusted amount. Second, the operative formula uses a bare "or" between the four percent (4%) floor and the applicable inflation index without specifying that Quintiles may elect the higher of the two figures, allowing the counterparty to argue the clause requires application of the lower metric; compounding this, the fallback reference to "the equivalent inflation index of the country where services are performed" is undefined, creating a further avenue to challenge the index selected by Quintiles and therefore the legitimacy of any increase. Left unaddressed, these gaps could allow the counterparty to withhold or dispute adjusted fees even where Quintiles' actual costs have risen materially.
suggestions.original_text: Inflation Adjustments. Where services in a Work Order are provided by Quintiles over multiple calendar years, Quintiles may increase its fees at the beginning of each calendar year to reflect increases in Quintiles’ business costs on a prospective basis only. Quintiles’ overall costs may be increased for the next twelve (12) month period using four percent (4%) or the average percentage change in the wages/earnings survey as published in the Economist (or as reported at www.economist.com) or the equivalent inflation index of the country where services are performed, over the preceding twelve (12) month period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Inflation Adjustments. Where services in a Work Order are provided by Quintiles over multiple calendar years, Quintiles may increase its fees effective January 1 of each calendar year to reflect increases in Quintiles' business costs on a prospective basis only, upon no less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party. Quintiles' overall costs may be increased for the next twelve (12) month period using the higher of four percent (4%) or the average percentage change in the wages/earnings survey as published in the Economist (or as reported at www.economist.com) or the officially published government consumer price index of the country where services are performed, over the preceding twelve (12) month period.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the assignment clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to material risk on multiple fronts: consent is absolute with no "not unreasonably withheld" standard and no response deadline, meaning Sponsor could withhold consent arbitrarily to block Quintiles from legitimate corporate restructurings or affiliate transfers. There is no change-of-control provision, so Sponsor could be acquired by a direct competitor of Quintiles with no termination right available. The clause is also silent on the assigning party's continuing liability and on notice obligations, leaving Quintiles without recourse against the original Sponsor if an uncreditworthy assignee fails to perform.
suggestions.original_text: Binding Agreement and Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of Sponsor and Quintiles and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Except as stated above in Section 17.1, neither party may assign any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement to any party without the express, written consent of the other party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Binding Agreement and Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of Sponsor and Quintiles and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Except as stated above in Section 17.1, neither party may assign any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that either party may, upon written notice to the non-assigning party, assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, in which case the assigning party shall remain liable for all obligations under this Agreement unless expressly released in writing by the other party. Either party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other party undergoes a change of control to a direct competitor of the terminating party.

suggestions.clause: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability
suggestions.reason: The waiver provision does not require a waiver to be in writing and signed by the waiving party, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed to arguments that it has informally waived a contractual right through conduct, course of dealing, or an oral statement. Without a written-waiver requirement, a counterparty could contend that Quintiles, Inc.'s failure to object to a non-conforming performance or repeated accommodation constitutes a binding relinquishment of rights, undermining Quintiles, Inc.'s ability to enforce the Agreement's terms at a later stage. This gap is particularly consequential in a Master Services Agreement, where operational interactions are frequent and informal communications between the parties are common.
suggestions.original_text: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability. This Agreement shall be construed, governed, interpreted, and applied in accordance with the laws of the State of New York exclusive of its conflicts of law provisions. The failure to enforce any right or provision herein shall not constitute a waiver of that right or provision. Any waiver of a breach of a provision shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach of that provision. If any provisions herein are found to be unenforceable on the grounds that they are overly broad or in conflict with applicable laws, it is the intent of the parties that such provisions be replaced, reformed or narrowed so that their original business purpose can be accomplished to the extent permitted by law, and that the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Choice of Law, Waiver and Enforceability. This Agreement shall be construed, governed, interpreted, and applied in accordance with the laws of the State of New York exclusive of its conflicts of law provisions. The failure to enforce any right or provision herein shall not constitute a waiver of that right or provision. No waiver of any right or provision shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by an authorized representative of the waiving party. Any waiver of a breach of a provision shall not constitute a waiver of any subsequent breach of that provision. If any provisions herein are found to be unenforceable on the grounds that they are overly broad or in conflict with applicable laws, it is the intent of the parties that such provisions be replaced, reformed or narrowed so that their original business purpose can be accomplished to the extent permitted by law, and that the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.

suggestions.reason: The survival clause fails to expressly preserve rights and liabilities that accrued prior to termination, meaning a counterparty could argue that Quintiles, Inc.'s indemnification claims, payment entitlements, or IP ownership rights arising during the term are extinguished upon termination before they are fully resolved. Additionally, the clause states no duration for which surviving obligations continue, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed to uncertainty regarding the enforceability of confidentiality, indemnification, and invention assignment protections if a counterparty later disputes whether those obligations remain operative. Together, these gaps create material litigation risk for Quintiles, Inc. with respect to its most commercially significant post-termination rights.
suggestions.original_text: Survival. The rights and obligations of Sponsor and Quintiles, which by intent or meaning have validity beyond such termination (including, but not limited to, rights with respect to inventions, confidentiality, publication, discoveries and improvements, indemnification and liability limitations) shall survive the termination of this Agreement or any Work Order.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Survival. The rights and obligations of Sponsor and Quintiles, which by intent or meaning have validity beyond such termination (including, but not limited to, rights with respect to inventions, confidentiality, publication, discoveries and improvements, indemnification and liability limitations), together with any rights or liabilities of either party that accrued prior to such termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement or any Work Order indefinitely.

suggestions.reason: The arbitration clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to material procedural and operational risk in four respects: it states no governing law, leaving Quintiles without a predictable legal framework to interpret its rights under the Agreement; it identifies the AAA office as the arbitral venue but does not designate it as the contractual seat, creating potential jurisdictional ambiguity; and it contains no pre-arbitration escalation step, no carve-out preserving Quintiles' right to seek emergency injunctive relief in court, and no obligation on either party to continue performing during a pending dispute, meaning a counterparty could strategically use arbitration as a basis to withhold performance without remedy. Taken together, these gaps leave Quintiles without basic procedural protections that are standard in market-form commercial arbitration clauses.
suggestions.original_text: Arbitration. Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the breach thereof shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (“AAA”) under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator shall be binding and may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. Such arbitration shall be filed and conducted at the office of the AAA closest to the Quintiles office having responsibility for the Project, and shall be conducted in English by one arbitrator mutually acceptable to the parties selected in accordance with AAA Rules. The arbitrator shall not have the power to award any punitive damages or any damages excluded by this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Arbitration. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of North Carolina, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Prior to initiating arbitration, the parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute through good faith senior executive negotiations for thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute. Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the breach thereof that remains unresolved following such period shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association ("AAA") under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator shall be binding and may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof. Such arbitration shall be filed and conducted at the office of the AAA closest to the Quintiles office having responsibility for the Project, which shall constitute the seat of arbitration, and shall be conducted in English by one arbitrator mutually acceptable to the parties selected in accordance with AAA Rules. The arbitrator shall not have the power to award any punitive damages or any damages excluded by this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction, and each party shall continue to perform its obligations under this Agreement pending final resolution of any dispute.

suggestions.reason: The supersession clause states that this Agreement replaces "all previous agreements (oral and written), negotiations and discussions" without expressly preserving liability for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation. Without a fraud carve-out, a counterparty could invoke the entire agreement provision to defeat a claim by Quintiles, Inc. that it was induced to enter into the Agreement, or any Work Order, through fraudulent misrepresentation made in pre-contractual negotiations. This is a material gap for Quintiles, Inc. because it would leave the company without recourse in precisely those circumstances where a remedy is most critical, and no other provision in the clause supplies this protection.
suggestions.original_text: Entire Agreement, Headings and Modification. This Agreement, together with the applicable Work Orders, contains the entire understandings of the parties with respect to the subject matter herein, and supersedes all previous agreements (oral and written), negotiations and discussions. The descriptive headings of the sections of this Agreement are inserted for convenience only and shall not control or affect the meaning or construction of any provision hereof. Any modifications to the provisions herein must be in writing and signed by the parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Entire Agreement, Headings and Modification. This Agreement, together with the applicable Work Orders, contains the entire understandings of the parties with respect to the subject matter herein, and supersedes all previous agreements (oral and written), negotiations and discussions, except that nothing in this Agreement shall exclude or limit the liability of either party for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation. The descriptive headings of the sections of this Agreement are inserted for convenience only and shall not control or affect the meaning or construction of any provision hereof. Any modifications to the provisions herein must be in writing and signed by the parties.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this Work Order template contains unfilled party and date placeholders, describes Quintiles' obligation only as performing "certain services" without any defined scope, and incorporates the Master Agreement by reference without limitation, exposing Quintiles to whatever uncapped liabilities, indemnities, or warranties exist in that document. The phrase "entered into from time-to-time" provides no mechanism, timing, or conditions governing when and how individual Work Orders become binding, leaving the scope and trigger of Quintiles' performance obligations commercially and legally indeterminate. The provision is also one-sided: it states Quintiles' performance obligation without any corresponding express acknowledgment of Sponsor's payment obligation, creating an asymmetric risk for Quintiles if a dispute arises over whether a binding Work Order was validly executed. The unlimited incorporation by reference is a document-wide cross-reference concern, as it may draw in Master Agreement provisions that subject Quintiles to broad indemnification or warranty exposure without the benefit of a liability cap carve-out at the Work Order level.
suggestions.original_text: This Work Order (“Work Order”) is between ________ (“Sponsor”) and ________ (“Quintiles”) and relates to the Master Services Agreement dated ________, (the “Master Agreement”), which is incorporated by reference herein. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles has agreed to perform certain services in accordance with written work orders, such as this one, entered into from time-to-time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: This Work Order ("Work Order") is between ________ ("Sponsor") and ________ ("Quintiles") and relates to the Master Services Agreement dated ________ (the "Master Agreement"), which is incorporated by reference herein, subject to the terms and conditions set forth therein. Pursuant to the Master Agreement, Quintiles shall perform the Services described in Exhibit A to this Work Order, and Sponsor shall pay the fees set forth therein, in each case in accordance with the terms of an executed written work order.

suggestions.reason: The clause establishes that this Work Order is "subject to" the Master Agreement but does not expressly state that the Master Agreement governs and controls in the event of a conflict with the Work Order, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed to a counterparty argument that work-order-level terms can override Master Agreement protections. More critically, the clause is entirely silent on the exclusion of extraneous terms — meaning a counterparty's standard terms, purchase orders, or online terms could be argued to form part of the contractual relationship, potentially displacing protections negotiated by Quintiles, Inc. in the Master Agreement. These two gaps, taken together, create material document-hierarchy risk that could be exploited to Quintiles, Inc.'s financial and operational detriment.
suggestions.original_text: Work Order. This document constitutes a “Work Order” under the Master Agreement and this Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Work Order. This document constitutes a "Work Order" under the Master Agreement. This Work Order and the services contemplated herein are subject to the terms and provisions of the Master Agreement, which shall govern and control in the event of any conflict with this Work Order, and no other terms or conditions shall apply.

suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause defers entirely to the attachments for all payment terms without anchoring any fee calculation methodology—whether fixed, time-and-materials, or usage-based—in the Work Order itself. For Quintiles, Inc., this creates a material financial risk: if an attachment is missing, disputed, or imprecisely drafted, there is no fallback standard within the operative clause to establish how fees are computed or what triggers a payment obligation. Without a minimum description of fee methodology at the Work Order level, Quintiles, Inc. is exposed to billing disputes and potential overcharges that cannot be resolved by reference to the governing text. This provision should be read alongside any payment milestone or invoice schedule in the attachments to confirm that the fee basis is fully and unambiguously documented.

suggestions.suggested_fix: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses. suggestions.clause: Services and Payment of Fees and Expenses
suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted is a bare list of attachment references with no operative payment terms, leaving Quintiles, Inc. exposed to significant financial and legal risk: there is no provision fixing fees or restricting unilateral changes, no invoice dispute mechanism to prevent a counterparty from withholding payment on pretextual grounds, no interest or suspension remedy protecting Quintiles, Inc. if payment is delayed, and no clarity on whether out-of-pocket expenses are reimbursable or require pre-approval. In the absence of these protections, a counterparty could dispute invoices indefinitely without consequence, refuse to reimburse expenses, or argue that fees are variable, all without any contractual remedy available to Quintiles, Inc. Any operative terms added should be read alongside Attachment 4 and the broader Agreement, and the survival clause should be reviewed to confirm payment obligations and accrued rights survive termination.
suggestions.original_text: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6
suggestions.suggested_fix: SCOPE OF WORK – ATTACHMENT 1; PROJECT BUDGET – ATTACHMENT 2; TIMELINE – ATTACHMENT 3; PAYMENT SCHEDULE – ATTACHMENT 4; TRANSFER OF OBLIGATIONS (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 5; LOCAL REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES (if applicable) – ATTACHMENT 6. suggestions.reason: The Term clause creates material operational and financial exposure for Quintiles, Inc. by deferring all termination mechanics entirely to the Master Agreement without independently stating grounds for termination, cure rights, notice periods, or consequences upon exit. If the Master Agreement is silent, ambiguous, or later disputed, Quintiles, Inc. would have no self-contained basis within this Work Order to terminate for the other party's material breach, to trigger a cure period before liability attaches, or to claim payment for services already performed. The absence of a written notice requirement and a defined effective date further compounds the risk by creating uncertainty over when any termination takes legal effect, potentially leaving Quintiles, Inc. obligated to continue performing or exposed to cost claims after a purported exit. The survival of applicable provisions following termination is also unaddressed, which may undermine Quintiles, Inc.'s ability to enforce payment, confidentiality, or IP rights after the Work Order ends.
suggestions.original_text: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is terminated in accordance with the Master Agreement. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is earlier terminated by either party: (i) for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other party; (ii) upon written notice if the other party materially breaches this Work Order and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days following written notice of such breach; or (iii) in accordance with the Master Agreement. Termination takes effect on the date stated in the terminating party's written notice, and upon termination Quintiles, Inc. shall be entitled to payment for all services performed through the effective date of termination. Provisions that by their nature survive termination shall do so. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until it is either terminated or completed.

suggestions.reason: The clause expressly binds Quintiles' corporate affiliates to all terms and conditions of the Master Agreement and this Work Order, but imposes no equivalent obligation on third-party subcontractors and consultants listed below. This creates a material gap for Quintiles, Inc.: if a subcontractor mishandles Sponsor's confidential information, breaches data protection requirements, or otherwise acts inconsistently with the Master Agreement, Quintiles, Inc. bears direct exposure to Sponsor for that breach without a corresponding contractual backstop against the subcontractor. This risk is compounded where the Master Agreement contains confidentiality, security, or data protection obligations that are expressly intended to flow through the supply chain. Any confidentiality or data protection survival obligations applicable to Quintiles, Inc. under the Master Agreement should be mirrored in Quintiles' agreements with its subcontractors to close this gap.
suggestions.original_text: Affiliates and Subcontractors. Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Work Order. Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles’ affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below:
suggestions.suggested_fix: Affiliates and Subcontractors. Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles' obligations under this Work Order. Any such affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of, and be entitled to all rights and protections afforded under, the Master Agreement and this Work Order. Any subcontractors or consultants (other than Quintiles' affiliates) that will be used by Quintiles in performing the Services are listed below, and Quintiles shall ensure that each such subcontractor or consultant is bound by written obligations at least as protective as those imposed on Quintiles under the Master Agreement and this Work Order with respect to confidentiality, data protection, and security.

suggestions.reason: The subcontractor provision is entirely unpopulated and contains no operative language establishing the conditions under which Quintiles, Inc. may engage subcontractors, leaving the clause legally deficient and unenforceable as written. The absence of any express statement that Quintiles remains responsible for its subcontractors' performance creates a gap that the counterparty could exploit to dispute Quintiles' accountability for subcontractor acts or omissions, exposing Quintiles to potential claims that it has disclaimed responsibility. Critically, the lack of a defined approval standard means the counterparty retains an implied unlimited veto over Quintiles' subcontractor selections, which could be used to obstruct Quintiles' operational delivery without justification; anchoring any consent right to a "not to be unreasonably withheld" standard protects Quintiles' ability to perform the Services without undue interference.
suggestions.original_text: [Insert names of any subcontractors or consultants, other than Quintiles’ affiliates, that will be used]
suggestions.suggested_fix: [To be agreed by the parties at execution.] Quintiles shall remain responsible for the acts and omissions of all such subcontractors and consultants as if performed by Quintiles directly. Any subcontractor or consultant not listed herein may only be engaged with the prior written consent of Client, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

suggestions.reason: The clause restricts its scope to "this Work Order," leaving modifications to the broader Master Services Agreement, schedules, and other exhibits potentially unaddressed by the amendment formality requirement, which exposes Quintiles, Inc. to disputes over whether informal changes to those related documents are binding. Additionally, the absence of any signing authority requirement means that a low-level employee or agent purportedly acting on behalf of the counterparty could execute a purported amendment, creating uncertainty and potential liability for Quintiles, Inc. if such an amendment is later claimed to be enforceable. Together, these gaps could undermine the integrity of Quintiles, Inc.'s negotiated contractual protections across the full scope of the engagement.
suggestions.original_text: Amendments. No modification, amendment, or waiver of this Work Order shall be effective unless in writing and duly executed and delivered by each party to the other.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Amendments. No modification, amendment, or waiver of this Work Order or any schedule or exhibit hereto shall be effective unless in writing and duly executed and delivered by an authorized representative of each party to the other.

suggestions.reason: The Currency Exchange clause as drafted is entirely an unfilled drafting placeholder, providing no operative mechanism whatsoever to govern how exchange rates are determined, when they are fixed, or who bears currency conversion costs — leaving Quintiles, Inc. with uncapped and unmitigated exposure to adverse foreign exchange movements on any cross-currency Work Order exceeding USD $1,000,000. Without a defined reference rate source, a fixed rate determination date, and a client reimbursement obligation, Quintiles, Inc. has no contractual basis to recover documented currency losses or conversion costs, and no court could determine the operative effect of this clause without resort to extrinsic evidence. The placeholder must be replaced with an operative provision before execution; until it is, Quintiles, Inc. should not execute any Work Order involving cross-currency fees or expenses.
suggestions.original_text: Currency Exchange. [Insert currency exchange provision in all Work Orders in which Quintiles will earn fees or incur expenses in excess of one million US. Dollars in a currency differing from the invoice and payment currency]
suggestions.suggested_fix: Currency Exchange. For each Work Order in which Quintiles will earn fees or incur expenses exceeding one million US Dollars (USD $1,000,000) in a currency other than the invoice and payment currency, the applicable conversion rate shall be the mid-market rate published by the Wall Street Journal on the date the relevant invoice is issued, and Client shall reimburse Quintiles for any documented currency conversion costs arising from such Work Order within thirty (30) days following receipt of Quintiles' written invoice therefor.

suggestions.reason: The Inflation and Cost Adjustment clause contains no operative text whatsoever — it is an unfilled placeholder — which means Quintiles, Inc. currently has no contractual right to adjust its fees over the term of the Agreement to account for inflation, rising labor costs, or increased input costs. For a services provider like Quintiles, Inc., this creates direct and material financial exposure across multi-year engagements where cost structures are likely to change materially. Without an express adjustment mechanism, Quintiles, Inc. would be required to negotiate any fee increase ad hoc, with no contractual basis to compel acceptance, leaving it locked into fixed pricing regardless of economic conditions.
suggestions.original_text: Inflation and Cost Adjustment. [Insert cost adjustment provision and inflation provision, if appropriate.]
suggestions.suggested_fix: Inflation and Cost Adjustment. Quintiles, Inc. may adjust the Fees applicable to any Statement of Work or Order Form on an annual basis by providing no less than sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. Any such adjustment shall not exceed the percentage change in the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) for the most recently published twelve (12)-month period preceding the date of such notice.
